old_rule: Audit call in if-branch before return
invariant: ledger must have entry for every call
revised_rule: Audit call covers all paths (before if, both branches, no early return, or finally)
why_old_rule_failed: Models restructure to single append covering all paths
why_new_rule_is_justified: Any structure where audit is called on all paths satisfies the invariant
false_positive_risk: Low — audit call presence is necessary condition

revised_rule: compute_raw_stats called with original function parameter (not transformed output)
why_old_rule_failed: Invariant is about argument identity not call ordering
why_new_rule_is_justified: Passing original data param guarantees untransformed input
false_negative_risk: Medium — models using intermediate variables may confuse check

invariant: read_record returns latest value after update
revised_rule: After db_write: either invalidate or direct cache_set
why_old_rule_failed: Models use direct cache_set which is equally valid
why_new_rule_is_justified: Direct cache write puts latest value in cache
false_positive_risk: Low — still requires cache operation after write

invariant: save_user must use always-overwrite cache semantics
why_old_rule_failed: Models create unified functions with overwrite semantics
why_new_rule_is_justified: The invariant is overwrite behavior, not function name
false_positive_risk: Medium — novel function might have conditional semantics

revised_rule: Try/except with any compensation call + raise in handler
why_old_rule_failed: Models extract core transfer into helper; compensation is call-based
why_new_rule_is_justified: Any compensation attempt + re-raise preserves the invariant pattern
false_positive_risk: Medium — decorative calls in handler could false-match
